title: Microsoft Agent 365: the control plane for agents
summary: Hold: the cost rationale puts the E7 price on top of prerequisite licences, although Microsoft's FAQ says E7 already includes E5 and Agent 365. The roadmap facts and documented control paths are supported; smaller corrections should acknowledge conflicting documentation and the optional source-platform delete permission.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connected platform synchronisation is manual through Sync agents and does not run on a schedule.
claims.quote: Manual synchronization only. Agent 365 doesn't currently sync on a schedule, and Microsoft doesn't prescribe a fixed synchronization interval.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Source-platform deletions are not guaranteed to remove registry entries and stale entries may need manual removal.
claims.quote: Synchronization doesn't currently guarantee that an agent removed from the source platform is automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.claim: Connected platform connections are read-only by design.
claims.quote:
Connected platform connections are read-only by design:
The only exception is an explicit administrator action to remove a synchronized agent, which requires a separate, optional delete permission that you can choose not to grant.
claims.fix: Add the qualification immediately after 'read-only by design': 'An explicit administrator removal can delete a synchronized agent at source if the connection has the separate optional delete permission; that permission can be withheld.' The qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/connected-platforms#security-model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Agent 365 never invokes, executes, or interacts with agents in the source platform.

claims.quote: Agent 365 stores the credentials that you enter for a connection as encrypted connection data within Microsoft 365. Microsoft encrypts the credentials at rest and in transit.

claims.quote: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential, such as an API key, secret, or private key.

claims.quote:
At least one user must be licensed with a qualifying Microsoft Agent 365 license to enable Agent 365.
You review and approve agents before you publish them to your organization, and you decide who can use them.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Advanced governance, security and observability layers require premium licensing rather than merely the included registry.
claims.quote: Premium capabilities such as advanced usage analytics, agent governance policies, security posture management, threat detection, and data security controls require an Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Both the $99/user/mo E7 route and the $15/user/mo stand-alone route are on top of qualifying prerequisite licences.
claims.quote: Licensing prerequisites do not impact Microsoft 365 E7 or other E7 components because E7 includes Microsoft 365 E5 and Agent 365, along with Microsoft 365 Copilot and Entra Suite.
claims.fix: Replace the cost rationale with: 'High. Premium capabilities need broad per-user licensing: Agent 365 is a $15/user/mo stand-alone add-on to qualifying prerequisite licences, or is included in Microsoft 365 E7 at $99/user/mo. E7 already includes Microsoft 365 E5 and Agent 365; its price is not an extra charge on top of separately purchased prerequisite licences.' Source: https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/faqs/122.

claims.claim: The AI administrator role alone does not authorise configuring Entra Conditional Access policies.
claims.quote: AI Administrators aren't authorized to configure Conditional Access policies or Microsoft Entra access package policies. These actions require a highly privileged administrator role with the appropriate Microsoft Graph permissions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to decide observability collection, but no controls row identifies that collection control.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'decide per connection whether Collect agent observability data stays on.' Controls[3] governs only 'Connections that synchronise agents from external platforms'; its note mentions the administrator role and manual synchronisation, not collection.
claims.fix: Expand the existing connections row's governing description to include per-connection observability collection. Its note should direct readers to create or edit a connection and select or clear 'Collect agent observability data', and state that this is a Frontier preview, enabled by default for new connections, with possible provider-side query charges. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/connected-platforms#agent-observability-data-collection-preview.
